semantic_core.text: At 03:14:10, a wind-blown branch struck a conductor on Synthetic North Feeder 22, causing a 4.1 kA phase-to-ground fault.
At 03:14:23, phase-overcurrent relay protection sent a trip signal to circuit breaker 52-N22, opening Synthetic North Feeder 22.
At 03:14:25, lockout relay 86-N22 latched and prevented circuit breaker 52-N22 from automatic reclosure.
At 03:15:27, after Synthetic LS-22F opened the faulted segment, the automation controller initialized the solid-state tie closure sequence.
A damaged gate-driver component left 4.2 V on the gate terminal for 12 ms, delaying block recovery of the phase-A triac.
At 03:18:40, the phase-A triac in Synthetic TS-22/23 failed to block at a current zero, so MT1-to-MT2 conduction continued after gate removal.
The controller's open indication came from gate-supply voltage zero, not from the independent 22/23-VM voltage monitor, which still indicated conduction.
Phase-B and phase-C triacs in Synthetic TS-22/23 blocked normally after their gate pulses ceased, so the fault was confined to phase A.
At 03:15:42, the loop controller closed Synthetic TS-22/23, re-energizing the unfaulted part of Synthetic North Feeder 22 from Synthetic South Feeder 23.
At 03:18:42, the controller considered Synthetic TS-22/23 open after stopping its gate pulses, but phase-A current remained at 310 A.
At 03:19:07, the operator closed circuit breaker 52-N22, paralleling Synthetic North and South feeders through the still-conducting phase-A triac.
At 03:19:09, circuit breaker 52-S23 tripped on directional overcurrent because measured current rose from 310 A to 2.0 kA within 40 ms.
At 03:19:11, lockout relay 86-S23 latched, interrupting Synthetic South Feeder 23 and all restored Synthetic North Feeder 22 load.
At 03:20:40, the independent voltage monitor 22/23-VM read 0.4 V between MT1 and MT2, disproving the controller's open-state indication for phase-A.
Energy unserved equaled 3.67 MWh, computed from pre-fault loads of 1.8 MW and 1.3 MW over 71 minutes.
At 03:21:15, an independent phase-rotation monitor on Synthetic North Feeder 22 recorded zero positive-sequence voltage, confirming no other source had restored it.
At 03:58, an operator de-energized the triac gate drive and manually verified that MT1-to-MT2 voltage reached 12.0 kV, proving forward blocking.
At 04:12, a field crew replaced the defective triac gate-driver board and the damaged MT1-to-MT2 voltage monitor on Synthetic TS-22/23.
At 04:31, engineering updated the controller logic to require independent voltage monitor 22/23-VM to read below 5 V before allowing a feeder breaker close.
At 05:20, technicians ran a controlled restoration test and verified all triac modules blocked before each circuit breaker closure.
